newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end higher but restrained by FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end higher but restrained by FOMC.

text.p: Swiss shares ended higher in a technical reaction to Monday's losses and from covering short positions, but uncertainty over the U.S. Federal Reserve's FOMC meeting kept a lid on the market, dealers said.
Dealers said an expected U.S. rate hike of 25 basis points was discounted in current prices, but market reaction was still unsure even if the Fed increases rates by 1/4 percent.
The Fed's interest rate decision is expected around 1815 GMT.
The Swiss Market Index (SMI) of leading shares added 25.1 points, or 0.69 percent, to 3,660.6 points.
Most shares could not hang on to the day's highest levels and trading volume was moderate.

Banks saw good demand. One trader said UBS and CS Holding were underpinned by next Monday's press conference of utility firm Elektrowatt. He said old rumours about a merger of Elektrowatt and Motor Columbus were revived.
CS Holding has a 44.9 stake in Elektrowatt, while utility firm Motor Columbus is majority-owned by UBS.
Most-active UBS bearer shares jumped 1.7 percent to 1,184 francs. CS Holding added 1.50 francs to 122.50.
Pharmaceuticals recovered a bit from Monday's slump, helped by foreign buying.
Ciba and Sandoz rose around 0.2 percent each after slipping on Monday on news their merger might be delayed. Roche cerfificates advanced 85 francs to 9,080.
Holderbank fell 11 francs to 876 as the market continued to show disappointment with Monday's half-year results and the compnay's forecast that 1996 net profit would at best only reach 1995 levels.
Some banks reduced Holderbank earnings estimates and downgraded their recommendations for the stocks.
Alusuisse ended up nearly two percent at 934 francs.
